decisions.priorControllingText: File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.

decisions.priorControllingText: The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects, inaccessible content, and unsupported formats. A supported subdivision cannot be replaced by one whole-file unit merely to make coverage vacuous. SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1 triggers a challenge when any one of these thresholds is exceeded: 1,048,576 stored bytes in one text or document artifact; 100 mechanically countable pages; 20 supplied files or archive members; 500 raw units; or 5,242,880 aggregate supplied bytes. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.

decisions.priorControllingText: The versioned source-class checklist derives from the closed generic class set — governing law and regulation; standards and specifications; controlling contracts and prior agreements; authoritative technical documentation; official registries and databases; scholarly and measurement literature; and project-supplied references — filtered by the Stage 01 objective and declared jurisdiction or system scope. Omitting an entire applicable class requires explicit reasoning and is challenged by the SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW. The contract also declares explicit stopping criteria: every registered location searched; query saturation, meaning no new candidate source in the final registered query round; authority-chain closure, meaning every authority cited by an accepted controlling source received a disposition; the declared date or version cutoff; a disposition for every inaccessible location; and the residual-risk statement. Search completion without every declared criterion is invalid.

decisions.priorControllingText: - HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.

decisions.priorControllingText: An optional archive is only a transport representation of the same logical container. It must use the registered deterministic archive profile and pass the archive safety rules. The current profile is closed-loop-archive-profile/1: a ZIP archive containing only STORE (uncompressed) entries, entries ordered by canonical-path unsigned byte order, the UTF-8 filename flag set, every timestamp fixed to 1980-01-01T00:00:00, no directory entries, no symlinks or special entries, no archive comment, no encryption, and no extra fields except a Zip64 field exactly where an entry or archive size requires it. The manifest is always at `manifest.json`; the authoritative prompt is at `instruction.txt`; an inbound response is at `response.json`. Directory entries, timestamps, permissions, compression method, compression level, and path normalization are fixed by the registered archive profile. An archive mismatch does not alter the logical package identity; it rejects the transport representation.

decisions.priorControllingText: Every artifact and package member is classified PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED, CREDENTIAL_SECRET, or UNKNOWN. CREDENTIAL_SECRET is never externally transferred. RESTRICTED or UNKNOWN content requires current recipient/provider suitability and human disclosure authorization. Package creation uses a derived allowlist, prohibited-member exclusion, known secret-pattern scan, path scan, disclosure check, and supported metadata inventory. A clean heuristic scan is not proof of absence. Redaction creates a new artifact and never silently replaces the original.

An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.

decisions.priorControllingText: The current registries are closed-loop-json-selector/1 and closed-loop-xml-selector/1. closed-loop-json-selector/1 MUST support at least: the root `$`; child access by identifier name and by single-quoted bracket name; nonnegative array index; and the wildcard `*` over object values and array elements. Selection order is document order. Recursive descent, filters, unions, slices, and script expressions are excluded from version 1. closed-loop-xml-selector/1 MUST support at least: absolute child-element paths from the document root; the element wildcard `*`; 1-based positional index predicates; attribute access `@name`; and `text()` value extraction. All other axes, predicates, and functions are excluded from version 1. A proposition that cannot be faithfully expressed within these registered subsets is not natively representable and routes externally.

decisions.priorControllingText: When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

decisions.priorControllingText: 5. For a supported external route, the author may provide an attributable semantic compatibility determination under ordinary agent authority. Support must include the current reviewed test's actual input/artifact/observation contract, the preserved fixture/defect evidence, and the reasoned target/outcome correspondence. Failure of any term leaves compatibility FALSE or UNKNOWN, as appropriate, and blocks admission. This conjunction qualifies the supported author's semantic judgment as EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED where that basis is established; the machine validates the binding and qualification facts and does not claim to prove arbitrary-prose semantic truth. decisions.priorControllingText: For every registered hash kind, the preimage inclusion set is exactly the canonical fields of the subject record or manifest, excluding only the digest field itself and every field whose value depends on that digest, fields declared audit-only or derived-summary, and fields the owning schema explicitly excludes with a registered reason. The scope-hash preimage is exactly the Section 14.7 dimensions of the operation, and the terminal-hash preimage is exactly the records enumerated in Section 36.9. An unregistered hash kind or pointer set is UNDEFINED_HASH_PREIMAGE and blocks the computation and every dependent gate. Default array semantics are ordered and order-significant; an array is set-valued only when its JSON pointer is explicitly registered with an element-identity key, a duplicate rule that rejects duplicates, and a sort rule of canonical byte order over the element identity. An unregistered pointer treated as a set is UNDEFINED_SET_SEMANTICS and blocks.

decisions.priorControllingText: Before the terminal Stage 30 calculation, the application creates a PRE_DELIVERY_CHECKPOINT bound to the exact Stage 27 through Stage 30 prerequisite records and every authorized artifact byte identity. The checkpoint is exported under the backup policy and its CHECKPOINT_ID is a terminal prerequisite and delivery-record field. The terminal prerequisite is satisfied only when the checkpoint custody state is at least BACKUP_EXPORT_ACTION_COMPLETED; BACKUP_PACKAGE_GENERATED alone is insufficient because an in-origin package is not an external backup. A later post-transfer checkpoint may be recorded but cannot retroactively satisfy preauthorization backup.

decisions.priorControllingText: A run execution attempt that ends REJECTED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED never counts toward the exactly-ten requirement and cannot satisfy any matrix cell. Its reservation reaches a terminal state, the same run target slot is re-reserved under Section 35.6, and the replacement attempt receives a new fresh context reserved for that run. The superseded context becomes historical, is excluded from the ten-distinct-context calculation, and its outputs cannot appear in any authorized input. Exactly the ten current accepted runs and their ten current distinct contexts satisfy Stage 11. An accepted run is never re-executed within the same iteration; a defect discovered in an accepted run routes through Stages 13-17.

decisions.priorControllingText: The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID, attempt ID, exact artifacts, byte hashes, operator action, intended recipient/destination/channel, device-reported time, result, and available external receipt. When the requested outcome includes delivery to the operator or another destination, Stage 30 workflow completion requires at least one successful authorized export or share attempt within the delivery record's scope. DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED permits the UI to say "Delivery authorized." It may say "Delivery attempted" only after the action receipt exists. It may say "Delivered" only when current evidence attributable to the recipient, destination, channel, or external system establishes transfer at its actual epistemic basis. The application cannot prevent or count transfers performed outside its controlled action path and must display that limitation. It does not claim it can undo a completed external transfer.
